title: Chapter 209: Why Are You Here Again?
html:
Freed from Xu Yin’s grip, the white figure retreated with astonishing speed.

“Don’t run!” Chen Ge refused to waste such an opportunity. Cleaver raised, he pursued. Without the woman’s control, the figure continued to weaken, its face and body growing increasingly indistinct.

Sensing danger, the monster darted to the black suitcase, snatched something from inside, and fled toward the front door. Chen Ge could not see the object clearly, but if the creature wanted it, he could not let it escape with it.

The cleaver had already wounded the white figure. Changing targets, Chen Ge slashed at the object in its grasp. When the creature dodged, he seized it.

Their struggle tore the object in two, and one half fluttered to the floor. Desperate to escape, the white figure abandoned it. Chen Ge pursued as far as the doorway, but the dark corridor stood empty. Reason prevailed: without Xu Yin’s help, he might lose if the creature cornered him.

He abandoned the chase, shut the door, and switched on the living-room lights. The sight made his eye twitch. The woman lay on the cold floor, limbs twisted at unnatural angles and eyes bulging as she screamed. Her hairless face held an incomprehensible mixture of agony, release, and joy.

“Does it hurt?” What happened to her now was Xu Yin’s affair. Chen Ge’s mission had been to find the woman and help the Tape Ghost fulfill his wish. He turned and picked up the torn paper.

It appeared to be a promotional flyer, though most of the information was on the half the white figure had taken. Chen Ge’s fragment contained only three red words and a short slogan. Ghost Stories Society? Share one true ghost story every week?

The fragment held his attention not only because the white figure had tried so desperately to save it, but because its background depicted a half-open blood-red door.

It’s about the world behind the door?

The flyer had belonged to Patient No. 2, someone who had crossed behind the door.

Did the escaped patients establish it? And what does “one true ghost story every week” mean?

The crude flyer and cryptic introduction made even loan advertisements pasted to telephone poles look informative.

Members must tell genuine ghost stories. What happens if someone has none? Do they invent one? How could the society tell truth from fiction?Chen Ge pocketed the fragment. His recent experiences could terrify any ordinary audience. If the listeners were ghosts, however, it was difficult to say who would frighten whom.

The woman’s screams gradually faded, replaced by a mechanical female voice repeating, “So painful…”

“Did he pull her into the tape?” Chen Ge approached. Her eyes were dull and lifeless, as though her soul had been drained away. He neither knew nor cared what Xu Yin had done; that reckoning belonged to them.

After placing her on the sofa, Chen Ge switched off the recorder. As he pressed the button, the black phone vibrated with a new message.

“Congratulations on completing Xu Yin’s wish. His opinion of you has greatly improved. Would you like to employ the Tape Ghost at the Haunted House?”

The Affection Mission is complete—just like that?

Xu Yin was more powerful than the Pen Spirit, and his affection mission had accordingly been far more dangerous.

“Would you like to employ the Tape Ghost at the Haunted House? Failure to answer within twenty-four hours will forfeit this opportunity.”

“Yes!” Chen Ge tapped the screen, his excitement beyond anything an ordinary person could understand.

“Congratulations, Specter’s Favored, you have hired a special-type Baleful Specter—Xu Yin.

“Xu Yin (Baleful Specter): He possesses a unique voice. (Can temporarily control lingering spirits and disrupt other Baleful Specters. Ineffective against Red Specters. Usable once per week.)

“Note: Xu Yin feeds on visitors’ terrified screams. Their fear will strengthen him, but if kept isolated and miserable, he may choose to leave.”

The description pleased Chen Ge. Like the Pen Spirit, Xu Yin was a special-type Baleful Specter with a distinctive ability.

Not bad. I have another trump card for future Trial Missions.

Chen Ge removed the cassette and placed it beside the ballpoint pen.

The only drawback is that Xu Yin appears only while the tape is playing. I’ll need to find a portable recorder at the flea market.

Only then did Chen Ge remember the other “victim” in the bathroom. He hurried inside and found Gu Feiyu completely unconscious.

I bet this will scar the young man for life.

He pulled Gu Feiyu from the bathtub, covered him with his uniform, buried the cleaver at the bottom of his backpack, and waited in the living room for Inspector Lee.

Twenty minutes later, Inspector Lee arrived with the landlord. To avoid panic, they entered quietly.

“Chen Ge!” Inspector Lee spotted him seated in the middle of the room. “Are you hurt? Where is the suspect?”

“Already tied up. The victim is the security guard; he’s still unconscious.”

Inspector Lee surveyed the scene, frowning. “The woman is the attacker, and the man is the victim?”

“Yes.”

“Why are you here? What is your role?”

“I…” Chen Ge blurted, “It was a coincidence. A girl on the fourteenth floor suffers from depression, and I’ve been helping her. I came to check on her tonight. If you don’t believe me, ask her mother.”

“So you stumbled onto an attempted murder entirely by accident?”

“I suppose.” The officers’ expressions changed as soon as he answered. “I’m serious. It was a coincidence.”

“You don’t have to explain. I believe you,” Inspector Lee said reassuringly.

“Ah Yong, call an ambulance. The victim needs treatment and examination. Everyone else, secure the scene and collect fingerprints. Don’t touch the drinks. A smaller attacker may rely on drugs to subdue a stronger victim, so preserve everything carefully.”

Inspector Lee’s experience allowed him to reconstruct part of the crime at a glance. Chen Ge stood silently to one side, the torn flyer clutched in his hand.
